chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) who said:
I asked him about a man who recites two surahs in one ruku', so he said: 'No, for each surah is a ruku'.'

key_terms.لِكُلِّ سُورَةٍ رَكْعَةٌ: for each surah is a ruku'

ai.seo_question: How many ruku' are counted if two surahs are recited in one bowing position?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential ruling that reciting two distinct surahs in a single rak'ah does not create two separate rak'ahs, but rather constitutes one unit of prayer with extended recitation. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition's emphasis on the structural integrity of the rak'ah, distinguishing between the number of bowing actions and the volume of Quranic recitation within them. This ruling ensures consistency in prayer calculations, preventing the inflation of rak'ah counts based solely on recitational choices.
